groups.title: Action Functions
groups.question: You are building a 'new project' form in Remix that shows field errors after submit. Explain how actions process forms and return errors.

followUps.The action Function and FormData: How does an action read submitted form data?
followUps.useActionData for Validation Feedback: How do validation errors get back to the form?

evidence.text: The action reads the request's FormData.
Fields are read with formData.get, not bracket notation.
Values arrive as strings or files and need validation and conversion.
The action returns error data instead of redirecting.
useActionData gives the component that data after submission.
The form shows each error next to its field.

groups.title: Progressive Enhancement
groups.question: Your forms do nothing until JavaScript loads, and a 'mark as done' toggle navigates to a new page. Explain Remix's approach to forms and non-navigating mutations.

followUps.Form vs form and JavaScript-Optional Des: How does Remix's Form work with and without JavaScript?

evidence.text: Form behaves like a normal HTML form without JavaScript.
With JavaScript, Remix submits it with fetch and updates the page without a full reload.
Relying on onClick handlers instead breaks the form without JavaScript.
useFetcher submits to actions or loaders without navigating.
It suits inline edits, toggles and buttons that stay on the page.
Each fetcher tracks its own state, so several can run at once.

groups.title: Optimistic UI
groups.question: Users click save twice because nothing indicates progress, and a todo checkbox waits a second before ticking. Explain pending and optimistic UI in Remix.

followUps.Optimistic Updates with useFetcher: How do you make a fetcher update feel instant?

evidence.text: useNavigation exposes whether the app is idle, submitting or loading.
It drives pending indicators like disabled buttons or progress bars.
No manual loading state is needed for navigations and form submissions.
fetcher.formData holds the submitted data before the server responds.
The UI renders that expected value immediately.
If the action fails, the UI falls back to the real data.

notEnough: Only saying the UI updates first.

groups.title: Method and Intent Handling
groups.question: One route needs to create, rename and delete projects, and refreshing after a successful save submits the form again. Explain how you handle multiple intents and redirects.

followUps.HTTP Methods in Remix Actions: How does one action handle create, update and delete?
followUps.Post/Redirect/Get Pattern: Why redirect after a successful action?

evidence.text: HTML forms only send GET or POST.
A hidden intent field tells the action which operation to run.
The action branches on the intent, validating each case.

notEnough: Only saying you use one action.

evidence.text: The action returns a redirect after success.
The browser then loads the next page with GET.
Refreshing no longer resubmits the form.
